methodological_rigor.justification: This is a phase I, open-label, non-randomized dose-escalation/expansion study (Parts I and J) combining two oral agents, which is appropriate for initial safety/PK characterization but limits causal efficacy claims (Methods: Trial design; Discussion limitations). The sample is small (n=29 across 8 centers) and there is no comparator arm; efficacy endpoints (ORR, CBR24, PFS) are therefore descriptive and subject to assessment bias. Analyses report proportions and medians with 95% CIs (Results: ORR/CBR24/PFS), but no power calculation, multiplicity control, or missing-data strategy is described.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design is a single-arm phase I dose-escalation/expansion trial without randomization or a control group, which maps to Oxford level of evidence 4 (Methods: Trial design; Results). Clinical relevance is direct because it evaluates a therapeutic combination in ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer with patient-level efficacy endpoints (ORR, CBR24, median PFS) and safety (CTCAE-graded AEs). The cohort is heavily pretreated (median two prior lines in the advanced setting; high prior CDK4/6 inhibitor and fulvestrant exposure), making the reported activity (e.g., ORR 37% in measurable disease; median PFS 8.3 months) potentially meaningful for later-phase development.

reporting_quality.justification: Given an interventional clinical trial design, CONSORT is the closest applicable standard, though key CONSORT elements for randomized trials are not applicable because the study is open-label and non-randomized (Methods: Trial design). The manuscript reports eligibility, treatment regimen, safety grading (CTCAE v4.03), data cut-off, baseline characteristics, and key efficacy endpoints with CIs (Methods/Results), but it does not describe a prespecified statistical analysis plan, handling of missing data, or any registration-linked protocol details beyond the NCT identifier. Data/code availability is limited in the normalized text; results frequently reference supplementary tables/figures at redacted locations, with no clear public repository or code release described.

novelty_literature.justification: The main novelty is testing a next-generation oral SERD (camizestrant) combined with an AKT inhibitor (capivasertib) in a clinically relevant, endocrine-resistant ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer population. However, both components and the pathway rationale are established (capivasertib has prior clinical evidence with fulvestrant; camizestrant has prior monotherapy/combination data), so this is best characterized as a meaningful but incremental extension into a new combination regimen. The ctDNA subgroup summaries (ESR1 mutation and PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alteration strata) add useful positioning but do not by themselves establish a new mechanism or practice-changing result.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is clearly organized with a concise abstract that states design, regimen, prior-treatment context, safety signals, and key efficacy estimates (CBR24 and median PFS). Methods and results provide concrete regimen details, eligibility criteria, and CTCAE-based safety reporting, and the efficacy section reports point estimates with 95% CIs and defines response confirmation (Results/Figure 2 caption text). Some interpretability depends on supplementary materials that are referenced but redacted in this corpus, which slightly limits standalone clarity.

key_strengths: Appropriate early-phase design with clear regimen description and CTCAE v4.03 safety grading in a multi-center cohort (Parts I and J combined).
Clinically relevant efficacy signals reported with confidence intervals (ORR 37% in measurable disease; CBR24 51.7%; median PFS 8.3 months).
Inclusion of ctDNA-based subgroup summaries (ESR1 mutations and PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations) to contextualize activity across molecular strata.
key_concerns: Non-randomized, open-label, single-arm phase I design with small sample size (n=29) limits inference on comparative efficacy and introduces potential assessment bias.
Statistical methods are largely descriptive and the manuscript does not detail a prespecified analysis plan, multiplicity considerations for subgrouping, or missing-data handling.
Reproducibility posture is unclear in the normalized text; key supporting details are deferred to redacted supplementary materials and no clear data/code repository is described.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solidly reported phase I safety/PK/efficacy signal paper with direct clinical relevance but inherently limited evidence strength and novelty; suitable for a mid-tier oncology journal pending minor clarifications of analysis and reporting details.
